title: What are Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) and Why Do They Matter to India's Markets?
description: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) are international individuals or groups who invest in Indian stocks, bonds, and other financial assets. They bring foreign .

faq.a: SEBI sets comprehensive rules for FPI registration, investment limits, disclosure requirements, and compliance to ensure transparency, fair trading practices, and overall stability in the Indian securities markets.

faq.q: Can an ordinary Indian become an FPI?
faq.a: No, FPI status is specifically for non-resident entities or individuals investing in India's financial markets. Indian residents invest as domestic investors, following different regulations.

faq.q: What is the difference between FPIs and NRIs investing in India?
faq.a: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are Indian citizens living abroad who invest in India, often through specific NRI investment schemes. FPIs are foreign entities or individuals who are not Indian citizens and invest under the FPI regulations.

faq.q: Do FPIs pay taxes in India?
faq.a: Yes, FPIs are subject to capital gains tax and other applicable taxes on their earnings from investments in India, in accordance with Indian tax laws and relevant bilateral tax treaties.

faq.q: Where can I track FPI activity?
faq.a: Daily, monthly, and other periodic FPI investment data, including inflows and outflows across different asset classes, is publicly released by the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and widely reported by financial news outlets.
